shloka_text: विसृज्य तु सुहृद्वर्गं बुद्ध्या निश्चित्य राघवः । समीपे द्वाःस्थमासीनमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.44.1 ।।
transliteration: visṛjya tu suhṛdvargaṃ buddhyā niścitya rāghavaḥ | samīpe dvāḥsthamāsīnamidaṃ vacanamabravīt || 7.44.1 ||
translation: विसृज्य having dismissed, तु indeed, सुहृद्वर्गम् the group of friends, बुद्ध्या with his intellect, निश्चित्य having resolved, राघवः Rama, समीपे nearby, द्वाःस्थम् the doorkeeper, आसीनम् seated, इदम् this, वचनम् word, अब्रवीत् he spoke.
explanation: Having dismissed his group of friends and having resolved with his intellect, Rama then spoke these words to the doorkeeper who was seated nearby.
comments: Rama summons his brothers Lakshmana, Bharata and Shatrughna -- coming, they are dismayed to find his face grief-stricken and tear-stained -- embracing them, Rama declares they are his very life and asks them to join him in weighing the grave matter that troubles him.

shloka_text: शीघ्रमानय सौमित्रिं लक्ष्मणं शुभलक्षणम् । भरतं च महाभागं शत्रुघ्नमपराजितम् ।। 7.44.2 ।।
transliteration: śīghramānaya saumitriṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣaṇam | bharataṃ ca mahābhāgaṃ śatrughnamaparājitam || 7.44.2 ||
translation: शीघ्रम् quickly, आनय bring, सौमित्रिं Saumitri, लक्ष्मणं Lakshmana, शुभलक्षणम् endowed with auspicious marks, भरतं Bharata, च and, महाभागं the highly fortunate one, शत्रुघ्नम् Shatrughna, अपराजितम् the unconquered
explanation: Bring quickly Lakshmana, the son of Sumitra and one with auspicious marks, and also Bharata, the highly fortunate one, and Shatrughna, the unconquered.

shloka_text: रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा द्वाःस्थो मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः । लक्ष्मणस्य गृहं गत्वा प्रविवेशानिवारितः ।। 7.44.3 ।।
transliteration: rāmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā dvāḥstho mūrdhni kṛtāñjaliḥ | lakṣmaṇasya gṛhaṃ gatvā praviveśānivāritaḥ || 7.44.3 ||
translation: रामस्य Rama's, वचनं word, श्रुत्वा having heard, द्वाःस्थो the doorkeeper, मूर्ध्नि on his head, कृताञ्जलिः having made an anjali, लक्ष्मणस्य Lakshmana's, गृहं house, गत्वा having gone, प्रविवेश entered, अनिवारितः unhindered
explanation: Having heard Rama's command, the doorkeeper, with folded hands placed on his head, went to Lakshmana's house and entered unhindered.

shloka_text: उवाच सुमहात्मानं वर्धयित्वा कृताञ्जलिः । द्रष्टुमिच्छति राजा त्वां गम्यतां तत्र मा चिरम् ।। 7.44.4 ।।
transliteration: uvāca sumahātmānaṃ vardhayitvā kṛtāñjaliḥ | draṣṭumicchati rājā tvāṃ gamyatāṃ tatra mā ciram || 7.44.4 ||
translation: उवाच he said, सुमहात्मानं to the great-souled one, वर्धयित्वा having greeted, कृताञ्जलिः with folded hands, द्रष्टुम् to see, इच्छति wishes, राजा the king, त्वां you, गम्यतां you should go, तत्र there, मा not, चिरम् delay
explanation: With folded hands, he greeted the great-souled Lakshmana and said, 'The king wishes to see you; go there without delay.'

shloka_text: बाढमित्येव सौमित्रिः श्रुत्वा राघवशासनम् । प्राद्रवद्रथमारुह्य राघवस्य निवेशनम् ।। 7.44.5 ।।
transliteration: bāḍhamityeva saumitriḥ śrutvā rāghavaśāsanam | prādravadrathamāruhya rāghavasya niveśanam || 7.44.5 ||
translation: बाढम् 'Alright', इति thus, एव indeed, सौमित्रिः Saumitri, श्रुत्वा having heard, राघवशासनम् Rama's command, प्राद्रवत् he hastened, रथम् chariot, आरुह्य having ascended, राघवस्य Rama's, निवेशनम् abode
explanation: Having heard Rama's command, Saumitri (Lakshmana) immediately said 'Alright' and hastened to Rama's abode, having mounted his chariot.

shloka_text: प्रयान्तं लक्ष्मणं दृष्ट्वा द्वाःस्थो भरतमन्तिकात् । उवाच भरतं तत्र वर्धयित्वा कृताञ्जलिः ।। 7.44.6 ।।
transliteration: prayāntaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā dvāḥstho bharatamantikāt | uvāca bharataṃ tatra vardhayitvā kṛtāñjaliḥ || 7.44.6 ||
translation: प्रयान्तं departing, लक्ष्मणं Lakshmana, दृष्ट्वा having seen, द्वाःस्थो the doorkeeper, भरतम् Bharata, अन्तिकात् from nearby, उवाच he said, भरतं to Bharata, तत्र there, वर्धयित्वा having greeted, कृताञ्जलिः with folded hands
explanation: Having seen Lakshmana departing, the doorkeeper, from nearby, then greeted Bharata with folded hands and spoke to him.

shloka_text: विनयावनतो भूत्वा राजा त्वां द्रष्टुमिच्छति । भरतस्तु वचःश्रुत्वा द्वाःस्थाद्रामसमीरितम् ।। 7.44.7 ।।
transliteration: vinayāvanato bhūtvā rājā tvāṃ draṣṭumicchati | bharatastu vacaḥśrutvā dvāḥsthādrāmasamīritam || 7.44.7 ||
translation: विनयावनतः humbly bowed, भूत्वा having become, राजा the king, त्वां you, द्रष्टुमिच्छति wishes to see. भरतस्तु But Bharata, वचःश्रुत्वा having heard the words, द्वाःस्थात् from the doorkeeper, रामसमीरितम् spoken by Rama.
explanation: The doorkeeper informed Bharata that the king, having become humble, wished to see him, and Bharata heard these words spoken by Rama through the doorkeeper.

shloka_text: उत्पपातासनात्तूर्णं पद्भ्यामेव ययौ बली । दृष्ट्वा प्रयान्तं भरतं त्वरमाणः कृताञ्जलिः ।। 7.44.8 ।।
transliteration: utpapātāsanāttūrṇaṃ padbhyāmeva yayau balī | dṛṣṭvā prayāntaṃ bharataṃ tvaramāṇaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ || 7.44.8 ||
translation: उत्पपात sprang up, आसनात् from his seat, तूर्णं quickly, पद्भ्यामेव by his feet alone, ययौ went, बली the mighty one (Bharata). दृष्ट्वा Having seen, प्रयान्तं going, भरतं Bharata, त्वरमाणः hurrying, कृताञ्जलिः with folded hands (the doorkeeper).
explanation: The mighty Bharata quickly sprang from his seat and went on foot, while the doorkeeper, seeing Bharata depart, hurried along with folded hands.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नभवनं गत्वा ततो वाक्यमुवाच ह । एह्यागच्छ रघुश्रेष्ठ राजा त्वां द्रष्टुमिच्छति ।। 7.44.9 ।।
transliteration: śatrughnabhavanaṃ gatvā tato vākyamuvāca ha | ehyāgaccha raghuśreṣṭha rājā tvāṃ draṣṭumicchati || 7.44.9 ||
translation: शत्रुघ्नभवनं to Shatrughna's abode, गत्वा having gone, ततो then, वाक्यमुवाच spoke words, ह indeed. एह्यागच्छ Come, come, रघुश्रेष्ठ O best of Raghus, राजा the king, त्वां you, द्रष्टुमिच्छति wishes to see.
explanation: The doorkeeper then went to Shatrughna's abode and spoke, saying, "Come, O best of Raghus, the king wishes to see you."

shloka_text: गतो हि लक्ष्मणः पूर्वं भरतश्च महायशाः । श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य शत्रुघ्नः परमासनात् ।। 7.44.10 ।।
transliteration: gato hi lakṣmaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ bharataśca mahāyaśāḥ | śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya śatrughnaḥ paramāsanāt || 7.44.10 ||
translation: गतो has gone, हि indeed, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, पूर्वं previously, भरतश्च and Bharata, महायशाः the greatly renowned. श्रुत्वा Having heard, तु but, वचनं the words, तस्य of him (the doorkeeper), शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, परमासनात् from his excellent seat.
explanation: The doorkeeper also informed Shatrughna that Lakshmana had already gone, and the greatly renowned Bharata too, and upon hearing these words, Shatrughna rose from his excellent seat.

shloka_text: शिरसा धरणीं प्राप्य प्रययौ यत्र राघवः । द्वाःस्थस्त्वागम्य रामाय सर्वानेव कृताञ्जलिः । निवेदयामास तदा भ्रातऽन्स्वान्समुपस्थितान् ।। 7.44.11 ।।
transliteration: śirasā dharaṇīṃ prāpya prayayau yatra rāghavaḥ | dvāḥsthastvāgamya rāmāya sarvāneva kṛtāñjaliḥ | nivedayāmāsa tadā bhrāta'nsvānsamupasthitān || 7.44.11 ||
translation: शिरसा with his head, धरणीं the ground, प्राप्य having touched, प्रययौ went, यत्र where, राघवः Rama. द्वाःस्थस्तु But the doorkeeper, आगम्य having come, रामाय to Rama, सर्वान् एव all of them indeed, कृताञ्जलिः with folded hands, निवेदयामास reported, तदा then, भ्रातॄन् his brothers, स्वान् his own, समुपस्थितान् having arrived.
explanation: Shatrughna, having bowed his head to the ground, went to where Rama was, and then the doorkeeper, with folded hands, reported to Rama that all his brothers had arrived.

shloka_text: कुमारानागताञ्छ्रुत्वा चिन्ताव्याकुलितेन्द्रियः । अवाङ्मुखो दीनमना द्वाःस्थं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.44.12 ।।
transliteration: kumārānāgatāñchrutvā cintāvyākulitendriyaḥ | avāṅmukho dīnamanā dvāḥsthaṃ vacanamabravīt || 7.44.12 ||
translation: कुमारानागतान् the princes arrived, श्रुत्वा having heard, चिन्ताव्याकुलितेन्द्रियः whose senses were agitated by worry, अवाङ्मुखः with a downcast face, दीनमनाः distressed in mind, द्वाःस्थम् to the doorkeeper, वचनम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having heard that the princes had arrived, Rama, with his senses agitated by worry, a downcast face, and a distressed mind, spoke to the doorkeeper.

shloka_text: प्रवेशय कुमारांस्त्वं मत्समीपं त्वरान्वितः । एतेषु जीवितं मह्यमेते प्राणाः प्रिया मम ।। 7.44.13 ।।
transliteration: praveśaya kumārāṃstvaṃ matsamīpaṃ tvarānvitaḥ | eteṣu jīvitaṃ mahyamete prāṇāḥ priyā mama || 7.44.13 ||
translation: प्रवेशय make them enter, कुमारान् the princes, त्वम् you, मत्समीपम् to my presence, त्वरान्वितः quickly, एतेषु in these, जीवितम् life, मह्यम् is mine, एते these, प्राणाः vital airs, प्रियाः dear, मम to me.
explanation: "You, quickly usher the princes into my presence, for my life is in them, and these are my dear vital breaths."

shloka_text: आज्ञप्तास्तु नरेन्द्रेण कुमाराः शक्रतेजसः । प्रह्वाः प्राञ्जलयो भूत्वा विविशुस्ते समाहिताः ।। 7.44.14 ।।
transliteration: ājñaptāstu narendreṇa kumārāḥ śakratejasaḥ | prahvāḥ prāñjalayo bhūtvā viviśuste samāhitāḥ || 7.44.14 ||
translation: आज्ञप्ताः commanded, तु indeed, नरेन्द्रेण by the king, कुमाराः the princes, शक्रतेजसः having the splendor of Indra, प्रह्वाः bowed down, प्राञ्जलयः with folded hands, भूत्वा having become, विविशुः entered, ते they, समाहिताः composed.
explanation: Commanded by the king, the princes, who possessed the splendor of Indra, entered composedly, having bowed down with folded hands.

shloka_text: ते तु दृष्ट्वा मुखं तस्य सग्रहं शशिनं यथा । सन्ध्यागतमिवादित्यं प्रभया परिवर्जितम् ।। 7.44.15 ।।
transliteration: te tu dṛṣṭvā mukhaṃ tasya sagrahaṃ śaśinaṃ yathā | sandhyāgatamivādityaṃ prabhayā parivarjitam || 7.44.15 ||
translation: ते they, तु indeed, दृष्ट्वा having seen, मुखम् the face, तस्य his, सग्रहम् eclipsed, शशिनम् the moon, यथा like, सन्ध्यागतम् set in the evening, इव like, आदित्यम् the sun, प्रभया by splendor, परिवर्जितम् devoid of.
explanation: They, having seen his face, which was like the moon eclipsed or the sun at dusk devoid of its splendor, were struck by his sorrowful appearance.

shloka_text: बाष्पपूर्णे च नयने दृष्ट्वा रामस्य धीमतः । हतशोभं यथा पद्मं मुखं वीक्ष्य च तस्य ते ।। 7.44.16 ।।
transliteration: bāṣpapūrṇe ca nayane dṛṣṭvā rāmasya dhīmataḥ | hataśobhaṃ yathā padmaṃ mukhaṃ vīkṣya ca tasya te || 7.44.16 ||
translation: बाष्पपूर्णे full of tears, च and, नयने eyes, दृष्ट्वा having seen, रामस्य of Rama, धीमतः the wise, हतशोभम् lost its beauty, यथा like, पद्मम् a lotus, मुखम् the face, वीक्ष्य having seen, च and, तस्य his, ते they.
explanation: And having seen the wise Rama's eyes full of tears, and his face, which was like a lotus that had lost its beauty, they were deeply affected.

shloka_text: ततो ऽभिवाद्य त्वरिताः पादौ रामस्य मूर्धभिः । तस्थुः समाहिताः सर्वे रामस्त्वश्रूण्यवर्तयत् ।। 7.44.17 ।।
transliteration: tato 'bhivādya tvaritāḥ pādau rāmasya mūrdhabhiḥ | tasthuḥ samāhitāḥ sarve rāmastvaśrūṇyavartayat || 7.44.17 ||
translation: ततः then, अभिवाद्य having saluted, त्वरिताः swiftly, पादौ the feet, रामस्य of Rama, मूर्धभिः with their heads, तस्थुः they stood, समाहिताः attentive, सर्वे all, रामः Rama, तु indeed, अश्रूणि tears, अवर्तयत् shed.
explanation: After swiftly saluting Rama's feet with their heads, all of them stood attentively, while Rama, in turn, shed tears.

shloka_text: तान्परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यामुत्थाप्य च महाबलः । आसनेष्वासतेत्युक्त्वा ततो वाक्यं जगाद ह ।। 7.44.18 ।।
transliteration: tānpariṣvajya bāhubhyāmutthāpya ca mahābalaḥ | āsaneṣvāsatetyuktvā tato vākyaṃ jagāda ha || 7.44.18 ||
translation: तान् them, परिष्वज्य having embraced, बाहुभ्याम् with his two arms, उत्थाप्य having raised up, च and, महाबलः the mighty one, आसनेषु on the seats, आसत sit, इति thus, उक्त्वा having said, ततः then, वाक्यम् a speech, जगाद spoke, ह indeed.
explanation: The mighty Rama, embracing them with his arms and raising them up, asked them to sit on their seats, and then he spoke these words.

shloka_text: भवन्तो मम सर्वस्वं भवन्तो जीवितं मम । भवद्भिश्च कृतं राज्यं पालयामि नरेश्वराः ।। 7.44.19 ।।
transliteration: bhavanto mama sarvasvaṃ bhavanto jīvitaṃ mama | bhavadbhiśca kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ pālayāmi nareśvarāḥ || 7.44.19 ||
translation: भवन्तः you, मम my, सर्वस्वम् all, भवन्तः you, जीवितम् life, मम my, भवद्भिः by you, च and, कृतम् established, राज्यम् kingdom, पालयामि I rule, नरेश्वराः O kings.
explanation: Rama declared to the kings that they were his everything and his very life, and that he ruled the kingdom which they had helped establish.

shloka_text: भवन्तः कृतशास्त्रार्था बुद्ध्या च परिनिष्ठिताः । सम्भूय च मदर्थो ऽयमन्वेष्टव्यो नरेश्वराः ।। 7.44.20 ।।
transliteration: bhavantaḥ kṛtaśāstrārthā buddhyā ca pariniṣṭhitāḥ | sambhūya ca madartho 'yamanveṣṭavyo nareśvarāḥ || 7.44.20 ||
translation: भवन्तः you, कृतशास्त्रार्थाः learned in scriptures, बुद्ध्या by intellect, च and, परिनिष्ठिताः perfected, सम्भूय having assembled, च and, मदर्थः my purpose, अयम् this, अन्वेष्टव्यः should be investigated, नरेश्वराः O kings.
explanation: Rama further stated that since they were learned in scriptures and perfected in intellect, they should all together investigate this matter of his.

shloka_text: तथा वदति काकुत्स्थे अवधानपरायणाः । उद्विग्नमनसः सर्वे किं नु राजाभिधास्यति ।। 7.44.21 ।।
transliteration: tathā vadati kākutsthe avadhānaparāyaṇāḥ | udvignamanasaḥ sarve kiṃ nu rājābhidhāsyati || 7.44.21 ||
translation: तथा thus, वदति while speaking, काकुत्स्थे by Kakutstha, अवधानपरायणाः very attentive, उद्विग्नमनसः with agitated minds, सर्वे all, किम् what, नु indeed, राजा the king, अभिधास्यति will say.
explanation: As Rama spoke thus, all the kings, though very attentive, became anxious in their minds, wondering what the king would say next. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुश्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः ।। 44 ।। Thus ends the forty-fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
